title: Gaussian elimination of continuous matrices on constant-rank neighbourhoods
statement: For a normed field E, topological space T and finite row and column sets, a matrix M of continuous E-valued functions having constant pointwise rank r has near each point an invertible r-minor. After any continuous pullback into that neighbourhood, M equals P times the reindexed identity-and-zero block matrix times Q, with determinants of P and Q units. For locally constant rank the same conclusion holds with a rank depending on the chosen neighbourhood. Zero rank and empty index sets are included.

proof.text: Use the finite-dimensional rank/minor criterion to choose an r-minor nonzero at the point; nonzero determinant forces the row and column selections injective. Its nonvanishing locus is open. Use the existing PadicAlgCl.sumComplEquiv and sumComplEquiv_symm_inl, extracted unchanged to the shared finite-index-splitting module, to identify the selected block.
A nowhere-zero continuous function is a unit: its reciprocal is continuous by inv_zero continuity away from zero. On any pullback to the chosen locus this makes the selected minor invertible.

Apply the source library Matrix.schur_eq_zero_of_rank_le to all evaluation homomorphisms. Evaluations jointly detect zero continuous functions, and the constant-rank bound kills the Schur complement. Matrix.exists_eq_mul_fromBlocks_one_zero gives P and Q; reindex back. Evaluation homomorphisms are abbreviations of Mathlib ContinuousMap.evalAlgHom over ℤ, forgetting its algebra structure.

For locally constant rank first choose a rank-constant open neighbourhood, apply the constant-rank theorem to its subspace, and take the open image of the resulting neighbourhood. Continuous maps into that image lift to the subspace.
